recentItems.title: Live: China’s Pinglu Canal set to open for navigation
recentItems.description:
Pinglu Canal in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region is set to open for navigation on September 16. It's the first river-to-sea canal planned and coordinated by the central government since 1949.
CMG reporters take you behind the scenes to explore the canal’s smart operations, waterway services and tourism offerings, as well as preparations for the opening.
Join us live as the Pinglu Canal opens for the first time.

recentItems.title: Marching on: From barriers to bridges
recentItems.description:
The year 2026 marks 90 years since the victorious conclusion of the Long March, one of modern China's most pivotal chapters. In the series Marching On, CGTN correspondents retrace the Long March route nationwide, unpacking the enduring legacy of its spirit in contemporary China. In this episode, reporter Alasdair Baverstock kicks off the journey across Guizhou's rugged hills and river‑carved valleys.

#longmarch #FrontlineStory

recentItems.title: Miles we share: Oranges and the road home
recentItems.description:
For Liu Yao's grandfather, a better life meant having enough to eat, the chance to study and a stable job. Growing up generations later, Liu says she had the security to have “more ambition.”

That ambition took her from Xingguo County in east China's Jiangxi Province to Britain, where she studied modern agricultural management. She eventually chose to return home, bringing what she had learned about management and marketing back to the orange groves. Today, her cooperative uses intelligent fruit-sorting equipment and e-commerce, including livestreaming, to sell its produce. In 2025, the cooperative processed and sold more than 5 million kilograms of navel oranges and helped more than 2,000 local people increase their incomes.

Liu is also a fourth-generation descendant of a Red Army soldier. In Xingguo County, where tens of thousands joined the army or fought during the revolutionary years, stories of leaving home reach back generations.

From her grandfather's hopes for a better life to her own journey away and back, Liu's story asks a quieter question: What if going back is also a way of moving forward?
